summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation continued a long-running technical project called "The Method 1.6," in which the person (M) and Claude are collaborating to review, verify, and maintain a large multi-volume mathematical/physics work stored across several large markdown files in Google Drive. The session began with Claude loading HANDOFF-17 (the prior session's handoff document) and executing a structured gate check against two live builds: BUILD90 main (1,983,081 B, md5 49065309b0c4fe8e055f693aed295cca) and BUILD91 compendia (2,483,858 B, md5 a450e062…). Claude then executed two planned tasks: seating working-register entry W-102 to produce BUILD92 compendia, and running a Phase R1 census instrument (census.py) over the six reader-facing member files to produce DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv (1,556 rows across classes C1–C13 covering unresolved pointers, unprinted theorem citations, withdrawn-figure survivals, R-FORM completeness, handle leaks, and more). The session closed with BUILD93 compendia (2,735,797 B, md5 842d1781d81d1f8bfb84d47b264033d5, 123 members) incorporating W-103 and five instrument files (census.py, DEFECT-CENSUS.tsv, minmax.py, numcheck.py, tower-2.py) as bundle members.

M explicitly identified a structural problem: every new chat session was repeating the same large overhead (folder listings, tarball downloads, inline base64 re-typing) before any subject-matter work could begin, meaning Phase R2 (the actual chapter-by-chapter read) never opened. When Claude acknowledged this and proposed two routes, M ruled Route 2: instruments travel as bundle members inside the compendia file rather than as separate Drive tarballs, because project knowledge cannot hold the volume of material this project requires and Drive remains the authoritative store. Claude executed this ruling immediately within the same chat rather than deferring it to the next session, producing BUILD93 and rewriting HANDOFF-18 accordingly. M's explicit correction was that the pattern of overhead repetition was unacceptable and must be structurally resolved, not merely noted.

The project's current state: no volume content has changed (beyond the WORKING-REGISTER.md entries W-102 and W-103); Phase R2 has not opened; chat 69's gate is now designed to fetch two files by title search, extract all instruments from members, and proceed directly to Part I, Chapter 1 without any folder listing, tarball download, or format-learning calls.

**Tool Knowledge**

For Google Drive searches, fetching files by exact title using `title = 'filename.md'` with pageSize 2 and excludeContentSnippets is substantially cheaper than listing a folder at pageSize 100, which consumed approximately a tenth of the context window for a check that needed only five file names. The pattern established for this project is: never use folder listing to locate known files; always use title search or a known file ID directly.

Large Drive file downloads spill to /mnt/user-data/tool_results/<tool_call_id>.json and must be decoded with `base64.b64decode(json.loads(json.load(open(p))[0]['text'])['content'], validate=True)`. Drive file metadata carries no md5 checksum, so verification requires downloading the file and computing the md5 locally. The shell environment is /bin/sh with no `time` builtin and no process substitution; `timeout 280` must wrap every potentially long-running python call; non-ASCII output must be processed through python or `iconv -c -t ascii//TRANSLIT` rather than piped through `cut -c`, which truncates on multi-byte characters.

The member extraction regex `^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>` with re.S|re.M is the established convention; the lazy group captures content including the trailing newline before the END FILE marker. The reverse-md5 guard (removing inserted content and checking the result against the prior build's md5) is the required integrity check for every build operation.
